page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding a standard general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware storage is integrated directly via a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, offering low-latency, high-throughput IO for ephemeral data processing. Networking capabilities provide a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps. The instance configuration operates without graphical processing hardware and assigns zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio and local NVMe storage, the configuration suits workloads needing fast scratch disks or cache storage alongside balanced compute capacity. Appropriate deployments include relational databases requiring temporary table space, distributed cache clusters, continuous integration nodes, ETL processing pipelines, and general web applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and dedicated Intel processors clocked at 3.9 GHz. It features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 16.0 GB of memory, which provides an even distribution of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The configuration includes 237 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage for high-speed scratch space and temporary file systems, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Designed without dedicated GPU hardware, the instance is intended for compute workloads that demand steady single-core frequency alongside high-speed local disk access. The balanced compute, memory, and direct-attached storage make the m8idb.xlarge well-suited for relational databases, transient data processing pipelines, caching tiers, continuous integration jobs, and containerized web application serving.
